rows.grounds: compound rodha+śakti+adhikāra; genitive singular expressing the sway of the obstructing power
locative of time indicating the period or moment
past passive participle used in locative absolute with kāle
indeclinable indicating spontaneity or absence of external agency
indeclinable particle marking contrast or emphasis
aṇu = the individual self, distinct from Śiva; genitive singular

items.question: What occurs for the individual self when the obstructing power's authority has run its course?
premises: The obstructing power exercises authority over the individual self for a period of time.
That period of authority can come to an end.
A change may then arise for the individual self without external intervention.
items.inference: When the time of the obstructing power's authority has passed, the relevant outcome occurs of itself for the individual self.
uncertainties: The sentence continues beyond this verse, so the specific outcome that occurs spontaneously is not stated here.
The precise force of svayaṃ in relation to grace or ripening remains context-dependent.
items.plain_english: But when the time of the authority of the obstructing power has passed, it happens of itself for the individual self.
